title: Forty-Eight Teams. Three Countries. One Time Zone You Actually Live In. The World Cup Starts Today.
excerpt: The 2026 FIFA World Cup kicks off in Mexico City with the biggest field in tournament history. Here is what NRIs in North America need to know.
body:
The FIFA World Cup begins today. Mexico faces South Africa at Mexico City Stadium at 3 p.m. ET — the first match of the largest World Cup in history. For the first time, 48 teams will compete across 104 matches in three countries: the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The tournament runs through July 19, when the final will be played at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

For the Indian diaspora in North America, this is not a theoretical event. The matches are being played in your cities.

## Three Opening Ceremonies, Three Countries

In another first, FIFA has scheduled three separate opening ceremonies — one in each host country. The Mexico ceremony begins at 1:30 p.m. ET today, ninety minutes before the opening match. Canada's ceremony takes place tomorrow at 1:30 p.m. ET in Toronto, ahead of Canada versus Bosnia and Herzegovina. The United States ceremony follows tomorrow evening at 7:30 p.m. ET at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, before the USA's opening fixture.

Fox Sports and Telemundo hold the broadcast rights in the United States. Streaming is available on Fubo, Peacock, Sling TV, and any live TV service carrying Fox or Telemundo.

## The First Week

Today's slate features two matches. Mexico–South Africa in Mexico City is followed by South Korea versus Czechia in Guadalajara at 10 p.m. ET. By the end of the first week, all 48 teams will have played at least one match.

The marquee fixtures come fast. Brazil faces Morocco in New Jersey on Saturday. The United States opens at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles on Friday. France takes on Senegal in New Jersey next Tuesday. England, Argentina, Spain, and Germany all play their first matches within the opening five days.

## What NRIs Should Know

Sixteen American cities are hosting matches, from Seattle to Miami. If you live near any of these metropolitan areas, live football is within driving distance: Los Angeles, San Francisco (Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara), Houston, Dallas, Kansas City, Atlanta, Boston (Foxborough), Philadelphia, New Jersey (MetLife), and Miami.

India is not in the tournament, but the diaspora's connection to global football is deep. The Premier League has a massive following among Indian Americans. This World Cup — hosted in their time zones, in their cities, at venues they know — removes the 3 a.m. alarm clock that defined previous tournaments.

## The Group Stage Schedule

Group stage matches run through June 27. The Round of 32 begins June 28. The Round of 16 follows on July 4–7. Quarterfinals are July 9–12, with semifinals on July 14–15.

Some fixtures NRI fans will want to mark: Brazil–Morocco (June 13, New Jersey), France–Senegal (June 16, New Jersey), Saudi Arabia–Uruguay (June 15, Miami), and Colombia–Portugal (June 27, Miami). The bronze final is in Miami on July 18, and the final is in New Jersey on July 19.

## Beyond the Ninety Minutes

For the estimated 745 million football fans in India — and the millions in the diaspora — this is the most accessible World Cup ever staged. The time zones are friendly. The cities are familiar. The streaming options are abundant. No World Cup has been easier for an Indian fan in North America to follow.

The last time the United States hosted the World Cup was in 1994. That tournament set attendance records that held for decades. This one, spread across three nations with sixteen more teams, is built to surpass every benchmark. And for the first time, you do not need to set an alarm to watch it.
